subject: northern harrier
title: This Hawk Has an Owl Face So It Can Hear Mice Hide

scenes.text: This hawk wears an owl's face, and it hunts with its ears.
The northern harrier glides low and slow over grassland, just above the tops of the plants.
Mice and voles hide under the grass, where eyes alone can't find them.
So its face has a disc of stiff feathers, like an owl, that funnels sound into its ears.
It hears the rustle, turns, and drops onto prey it never saw.
Males may feed up to five mates, dropping food to them in mid-air.

description:
The northern harrier hunts low over grassland and has an owl-like facial disc of feathers that directs sound to its ears, so it can find mice and voles hidden in vegetation.
A male can have up to five mates in a season and passes prey to the female in mid-air.

first_comment: In winter, up to 80 or 90 harriers can roost together on the ground. Hawk or owl: which is the better hunter?
